model.cityflow.int_trip_geography.name: int_trip_geography
model.cityflow.int_trip_geography.description: Trips with both zone endpoints resolved against the zone dimension. Kept separate from fct_trip because it holds one policy, stated once: an unresolvable zone id is treated exactly like the TLC's own unknown codes. Ephemeral, so it costs no storage and no second pass over the trips.

model.cityflow.mart_source_freshness.name: mart_source_freshness
model.cityflow.mart_source_freshness.description: One row per service and source period, with what was read and when. has_gap marks a month whose predecessor is missing, so the panel can break the line instead of drawing a smooth slope across a hole in the source.

model.cityflow.fct_trip.name: fct_trip
model.cityflow.fct_trip.description: One row per trip, incremental by source period. Every measure the dashboard shows starts here.

model.cityflow.mart_quarantine.name: mart_quarantine
model.cityflow.mart_quarantine.description: What the ingest removed, by rule, service and month, as a share of the rows the source held. The share is the comparable number.

model.cityflow.dim_hour.name: dim_hour
model.cityflow.dim_hour.description: Twenty four rows. The daypart bands are the ones the peak surcharge uses.

model.cityflow.mart_null_rates.name: mart_null_rates
model.cityflow.mart_null_rates.description: Null share per watched column, service and month. A null share of exactly 1.0 followed by a drop is a column being introduced, not a data quality problem: congestion_surcharge appears in 2019-02, airport_fee in 2022-01, cbd_congestion_fee in 2025-01, and passenger_count and ratecode_id are absent from the high volume for hire vehicle schema entirely. What should raise an alarm is a share that moves in the middle of a service's history, because that is a source that changed shape without announcing it.

model.cityflow.dim_ratecode.name: dim_ratecode
model.cityflow.dim_ratecode.description: The TLC rate codes 1 to 6 and the unknown code 99, plus member 0 for not applicable. For hire vehicle trips carry no rate code at all, so without an explicit member for that they would join to nothing and vanish from every rate code breakdown while still counting in the total. is_flat_rate marks the two negotiated airport rates, JFK and Newark, where the fare is fixed and the meter is not the story.

model.cityflow.dim_zone.name: dim_zone
model.cityflow.dim_zone.description: One row per TLC taxi zone, 265 of them, 260 with a polygon. Two separate things make a zone unmappable and the map has to tell them apart. is_unknown marks zones 264 and 265, the TLC's codes for a location that was never resolved: real trips, real money, no place. has_geometry false with is_unknown false marks zones 57, 104 and 105, real places the trip records can name that the shapefile does not carry. Anything drawn on a map filters on has_geometry; anything reporting unresolved location reads is_unknown. Neither is ever dropped from a total.

model.cityflow.dim_date.name: dim_date
model.cityflow.dim_date.description: One row per day in the build window, generated from the fact so it cannot fall behind it. day_of_week is 0 for Sunday, matching DuckDB's dayofweek, so nobody has to convert between two conventions.

model.cityflow.dim_service.name: dim_service
model.cityflow.dim_service.description: The three services the warehouse covers, written out rather than discovered.

model.cityflow.stg_zones.name: stg_zones
model.cityflow.stg_zones.description: One row per zone, 265 of them, with the seed's integer flags cast to boolean. Nothing else happens here: the ingest owns the geometry.

model.cityflow.stg_trips.name: stg_trips
model.cityflow.stg_trips.description: One row per clean trip with the four derivations every consumer needs. This is the row count the whole project is measured against: fct_trip has to match it exactly.

model.cityflow.stg_quarantine.name: stg_quarantine
model.cityflow.stg_quarantine.description: Rows the ingest removed, by rule and by source period.

model.cityflow.stg_source_audit.name: stg_source_audit
model.cityflow.stg_source_audit.description: What the ingest actually read, per service and source period.

seed.cityflow.holiday.name: holiday
seed.cityflow.holiday.description: Holiday dates with the name each one is published under. Generated from the statutory rules once and committed, so the list is reviewable in a diff rather than recomputed on every run. A fixed date holiday that falls at a weekend contributes a second row for the observed date, because the day offices and schools close is the day street demand moves.

seed.cityflow.zone_lookup.name: zone_lookup
seed.cityflow.zone_lookup.description: The TLC taxi zone reference, one row per zone id 1 to 265. Named zone_lookup rather than dim_zone because dbt resolves seeds and models in one namespace and the dimension of that name is built in the marts layer. Generated by the ingest from the published shapefile, which dissolves the polygons of a multi part zone into one.

source.cityflow.warehouse.stg_trip.name: stg_trip
source.cityflow.warehouse.stg_trip.description: One row per trip that survived quarantine, normalized across eleven published schema vintages. The natural key is trip_id, assigned by the ingest, because the TLC publishes no trip identifier.

source.cityflow.warehouse.quarantine_log.name: quarantine_log
source.cityflow.warehouse.quarantine_log.description: Rows removed, counted by rule and by source period. A rule that suddenly removes ten times its usual share is the first sign that an upstream schema moved.

source.cityflow.warehouse.source_audit.name: source_audit
source.cityflow.warehouse.source_audit.description: One row per service per source period per ingest, with the row counts and byte counts the ingest saw. This is the only record of what was actually read, as opposed to what was expected.

exposures.name: panel_pulse
exposures.label: Pulse
exposures.description: How many trips is the city taking, and when? Volume by day, by hour of the week and across the year, split by service, with holidays marked because a holiday Tuesday does not behave like a working Tuesday.

exposures.name: panel_geography
exposures.label: Geography
exposures.description: Where do trips start and end? Zone and borough volume on the map, airport traffic called out separately, and an explicit count of the trips whose location was never recorded, which are excluded from the map but never from the totals.

exposures.name: panel_trip_behavior
exposures.label: Trip behavior
exposures.description: What does a trip look like? Distance, duration and implied speed by hour and daypart, and what share of a fare is a tip, computed only over the trips where a tip can actually be seen.

exposures.name: panel_service_mix
exposures.label: Service mix
exposures.description: Who is carrying the city? The month by month split between yellow, green and high volume for hire vehicles, and how a fare divides into fare, surcharge, toll and tip differently in each.

exposures.name: panel_data_health
exposures.label: Data health
exposures.description: What did not make it, and what changed shape? Rows removed by each quarantine rule as a share of the source, which months are missing, and which columns are null for a whole month because they had not been introduced yet.

exposures.name: panel_metric_lineage
exposures.label: Metric lineage
exposures.description: For any number on the other panels, how was it made? Each metric traced back through the fact to the staging column and the source field it came from, including the rule that decides when a tip is a number and when it is a missing value.
